perspective:
From Christian Mensah’s available perspective:

- Christian is a Black male police officer. He has been close friends with Jonathan Balogun since childhood, often seeks Jonathan’s advice, and knows Jonathan is a carpenter with a master’s degree.
- Lately, Christian noticed Jonathan acting differently. He felt Jonathan was hiding something important, became anxious and suspicious, and arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- At the meeting, Christian told Jonathan he felt he was hiding something. Jonathan first asked why Christian thought that and said Christian could trust him, but then admitted he had been keeping something from Christian: he was in some trouble and had not known how to tell him.
- Christian told Jonathan he was worried and offered to help, saying they could face it together. Jonathan said the situation was complicated and he did not want to drag Christian into it, but then accepted that he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian asked whether Jonathan’s trouble was related to anything illegal. Jonathan said he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian said he understood, wanted Jonathan to be safe, and would look into the matter discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe Jonathan was being framed and that someone was trying to set him up. He told Jonathan he believed this, said he was not sure yet who was responsible but had leads, and decided to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence. Jonathan thanked him.
- Christian later found out who was behind it: someone both he and Jonathan know and trust. He felt betrayed and resolute. He told Jonathan this and said he would confront the person and make sure they were brought to justice. Jonathan warned him the person is dangerous but said he trusted Christian to do what is right.

Christian does not have access to details not observed, heard, or told to him—such as the exact nature of Jonathan’s trouble, the specific illegal activity, the name of the real culprit in the provided dialogue, the details of his leads/evidence, or Jonathan’s private thoughts beyond what Jonathan stated.
